definitions.explanation: The rise and fall of pitch in speech or music. Refers to the natural variation in tone that makes speech or performance expressive and engaging.

examples.japanese: {抑揚|よくよう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけて→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{話|はな}し{方|かた}→話し方：15767_hanashikata⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{抑揚|よくよう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦なくて→ない：01118_nai⟧⟦{眠|ねむ}く→眠い：00872_nemui⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: His way of speaking has no inflection and makes you sleepy.

examples.japanese: ⟦{朗読|ろうどく}→朗読：14875_roudoku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{時|とき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{抑揚|よくよう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{意識|いしき}する→意識する：17974_ishikisuru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{聞|き}き{手|て}→聞き手：19792_kikite⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{伝|つた}わり→伝わる：01961_tsutawaru⟧やすく⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: When reading aloud, being conscious of your intonation makes it easier for the listener to follow.

notes:
{抑揚|よくよう} literally means "suppression and raising" — the lowering and raising of pitch. It is commonly discussed in the context of public speaking, language learning, and music.

ETYMOLOGY: {抑|よく} (to suppress, lower) + {揚|よう} (to raise, lift).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抑揚|よくよう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つける→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧: to add inflection, to modulate one's voice
- {抑揚|よくよう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ない→ない：01118_nai⟧: monotone, flat (lacking variation in pitch)
- {抑揚|よくよう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦{話|はな}し{方|かた}→話し方：15767_hanashikata⟧: an expressive way of speaking
- {抑揚|よくよう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{富|と}む→富む：12343_tomu⟧: rich in modulation

NOTE: Japanese is often described by linguists as having less dramatic {抑揚|よくよう} than languages like English or Italian. Learners are sometimes told their Japanese sounds unnatural because they carry over the strong intonation patterns of their native language.
